title: Rochdale selected for £9.4m children’s mental health pilot
excerpt: Breaking: Rochdale will join Stockport and Tameside in Care Together, bringing NHS mental health professionals into children’s social care teams from early 2027.
body:
Rochdale has been selected for a new government mental health pilot designed to make support easier to access for children involved with social care and their families.

The Department of Health and Social Care has announced up to £9.4 million over three years for Care Together, which will operate across Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside.

Mental health professionals from existing NHS services will work within children's social care teams. The aim is to help families receive expert support earlier, with less difficulty navigating separate services.

NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board will lead the programme alongside the three local authorities. It is expected to launch in early 2027 and run until 2029.

Who could benefit?

The department says up to 7,000 children and young people across the three participating boroughs could be covered, alongside their parents, carers and guardians. That figure covers all three boroughs combined. A separate allocation for Rochdale has not been provided in the announcement.

The groups identified include children in need, those on child protection plans, children in care, care leavers and adopted children.

Support could include family therapy and help for parents and primary caregivers, with services tailored to individual needs.

What will change for families?

Mental health professionals will work within social care settings, bringing expertise into the teams already supporting children and families.

The government hopes this will make it easier to identify needs and arrange appropriate help before problems reach crisis point. Faster access is an intended benefit of the pilot, with its effectiveness to be evaluated during the programme.

Dame Diana Johnson, Minister of State for Public Health and Patient Safety, said:

“For too long, fragmented mental health services have left young people in care, care leavers, parents, carers, and guardians not knowing where to turn for support.

“We are committed to change how we support young people, and this exciting and innovative pilot will see thousands more children across Greater Manchester get specialist mental health support based on their personal needs and in quicker time, before they reach crisis point.”

Children's Minister Josh MacAlister said children supported by social care can face severe mental health challenges because of trauma and adversity. He said the pilot forms part of wider efforts to support vulnerable young people as they move into adult life.

Professor Manisha Kumar, Chief Clinical Officer at NHS Greater Manchester, said the programme would help partners provide earlier support that takes account of children's experiences and wider family circumstances.

She said learning from the work in Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside would also help shape changes nationally.

When will Care Together start?

The pilot is expected to launch in early 2027 and run until 2029. An evaluation will assess whether the approach could be extended to other parts of the country.

The announcement does not yet specify how many Rochdale families will receive support, how referrals will work or which local teams will take part.

For local families, those practical details will matter: who can access help, how quickly it becomes available and whether bringing services together makes support easier to obtain.

What would make the biggest difference to mental health support for children and families in Rochdale? Share your thoughts in the comments, while protecting children's privacy and avoiding details that could identify them.

Source: Department of Health and Social Care announcement supplied to Rochdale Daily.
